To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Os isotope ratios in arc lavas are always controlled by a binary mixing process between a mantle component and a radiogenic component, and that the nature of the radiogenic component is variable from one arc to another.

Os isotope ratios are linearly correlated to the inverse of Os contents in arc lavas and this relationship can be explained by mixing between two components, a subducted component with a radiogenic signature, and a mantle component with unradiogenic signature.
Os isotope ratios in arc lavas reflect a binary mixing relationship between a mantle and an enriched component, which is not compatible with a single shallow-level crustal contamination process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin of the observed Os isotopic variability and the nature of the subducted components that control the isotopic composition of the source.
the geochemistry of the elements of the platinum group (Os, Ir, Pt, Rh, Ru, Pd), and the rare earth elements.
the origin of the Os isotopic variations in arc lavas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Os isotopes are a powerful tool to investigate the source of arc magmas and that Os isotopes and Os contents are controlled by a binary mixing process between two end-members, the mantle and the subducting slab.
the observed Os isotopic systematics in arc magmas is best explained by a combination of mantle peridotites and subducted sediments and/or altered oceanic crust.
Os isotopes in arc lavas are controlled by a binary mixing process between a mantle component and an enriched component, but the nature of the latter remains to be elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Os isotopes are useful tracers to understand the nature of the mantle wedge.
the Os isotopes are very useful in constraining the origin of the radiogenic components in arc lavas and the nature of the mantle wedge, which is the main source of these lavas.
Os isotopic compositions are a powerful tool to investigate the source of mantle-derived magmas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Os isotopes can be used to constrain the relative proportions of the mantle and slab components in arc magmas.
the Os isotope compositions of arc lavas reflect a mixing between mantle and subducted components.
the Os isotopes are very sensitive to the composition of the slab.
